project_reference.core_research_question: Can zero-point energy of the quantum vacuum be extracted as usable work through cyclic processes involving boundary condition changes?

scope.question: Can zero-point energy of the quantum vacuum be extracted as usable work through cyclic processes involving boundary condition changes?
in_scope: T=0 and finite-T Casimir energy and force for parallel plates
Quasi-static plate separation cycles with full thermodynamic analysis
Three no-go arguments (thermodynamic, Lorentz invariance, passivity) with explicit assumptions
Four loophole classes: boundary condition changes, topology changes, non-equilibrium states, dynamic Casimir
Extension to sphere-plate geometry as stretch goal
unresolved_questions: Which reference is the definitive formulation of the passivity theorem for QFT vacuum states?
What is the correct energy accounting for the dynamic Casimir effect — is photon production from vacuum genuinely 'extraction'?
Whether topology changes (creating/removing a cavity) constitute a distinct loophole or reduce to boundary condition changes

user_asserted_anchors: Casimir force F = -pi^2 hbar c / (240 a^4) for ideal parallel plates at T=0
Lifshitz formula for finite-T and real-material Casimir force
context_gaps: Definitive reference for passivity of quantum vacuum states not yet identified
Benchmark reference for dynamic Casimir photon spectrum not yet selected
crucial_inputs: Energy budget must account for every joule in the cycle
W_net parameter sweep must cover (a_min, a_max, T) space
Energy budget and parameter sweep must agree on sign of W_net
Three no-go arguments must give consistent assumptions or inconsistency is itself a result

formulations: QFT vacuum energy with boundary conditions (Casimir framework)
Thermodynamic free energy analysis of cyclic processes
Quantum passivity and the structure of the vacuum state
stop_and_rethink_conditions: W_net > 0 found in quasi-static regime — verify before claiming loophole
Three no-go arguments give inconsistent assumptions
Realistic material properties qualitatively change the conclusion vs ideal conductors

observables.name: Net work per cycle W_net
observables.definition: Total work extracted minus work input over one complete quasi-static plate separation cycle, as a function of cycle parameters (a_min, a_max, T)

observables.name: Casimir force F(a)
observables.definition: Force between parallel plates as function of separation, for ideal and realistic materials at T=0 and finite T

observables.name: Helmholtz free energy F(a,T)
observables.definition: Helmholtz free energy of the plate system as function of separation and temperature

observables.name: No-go theorem assumption set
observables.definition: The explicit set of assumptions required by each of the three no-go arguments, and whether they are consistent

claims.statement: A complete quasi-static Casimir plate cycle yields W_net <= 0, meaning no net work can be extracted from ZPE via this mechanism
Three independent no-go arguments (thermodynamic, Lorentz invariance, passivity) give consistent conclusions under overlapping assumptions
Four potential loopholes (boundary changes, topology, non-equilibrium, dynamic Casimir) are tested against the no-go assumptions and classified as genuine or apparent

deliverables.description: Complete energy budget for quasi-static parallel plate Casimir cycle showing where every joule goes
Parameter sweep plot of W_net vs (a_min, a_max, T) showing sign of net work everywhere
Formal derivation of three no-go arguments with explicit assumption lists and consistency analysis
Analysis of four potential loopholes tested against no-go theorem assumptions
Reproduction of known Casimir force and Lifshitz formula as validation benchmark

acceptance_tests.subject: claim-cycle-work
acceptance_tests.procedure: Verify energy budget (table) and W_net parameter sweep (figure) agree on sign of net work for all tested parameter values
acceptance_tests.pass_condition: No parameter point where energy budget says W_net > 0 but sweep says W_net <= 0 or vice versa

acceptance_tests.subject: claim-cycle-work
acceptance_tests.procedure: Compare computed Casimir force against F = -pi^2 hbar c / (240 a^4) for ideal plates at T=0
acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Relative error < 1e-6 for ideal plates; reproduce Lifshitz formula within numerical precision for realistic materials

acceptance_tests.subject: claim-nogo-consistency
acceptance_tests.procedure: Check that the three no-go arguments do not require mutually contradictory assumptions
acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Assumptions form a consistent set, or any inconsistency is identified and explained

acceptance_tests.subject: claim-loophole-analysis
acceptance_tests.procedure: For each loophole, verify complete energy accounting including all costs (work to change boundaries, radiation losses, etc.)
acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Each loophole has a definitive verdict (genuine or apparent) supported by energy accounting

references.locator: H.B.G. Casimir, Proc. K. Ned. Akad. Wet. 51, 793 (1948)
references.why_it_matters: Defines the ideal parallel-plate Casimir force F = -pi^2 hbar c / (240 a^4) that must be reproduced
Finite-temperature, real-material Casimir force formula — essential benchmark for realistic material calculations

forbidden_proxies.subject: claim-cycle-work
forbidden_proxies.proxy: Showing the Casimir force is attractive between plates
forbidden_proxies.reason: Attractive force does not imply net work extraction over a complete cycle

forbidden_proxies.subject: claim-cycle-work
forbidden_proxies.proxy: Reproducing Casimir energy E(a) without analyzing a complete thermodynamic cycle
forbidden_proxies.reason: Static energy calculation does not address whether cyclic extraction is possible

forbidden_proxies.subject: claim-cycle-work
forbidden_proxies.proxy: One-shot energy release when plates collapse without accounting for separation cost
forbidden_proxies.reason: Cycle must close — total work includes cost to restore initial configuration

weakest_anchors: Passivity theorem reference — definitive formulation for QFT vacuum not yet identified
Whether dynamic Casimir photon production constitutes genuine ZPE extraction or is powered by the mirror's kinetic energy
unvalidated_assumptions: Quasi-static approximation valid for the plate separation cycle
Perfect conductor boundary conditions capture the essential physics before material corrections
competing_explanations: Some authors (Puthoff, SED community) argue ZPE is extractable — our analysis should be able to identify where their reasoning diverges from standard QFT
disconfirming_observations: W_net > 0 found in quasi-static regime would indicate a genuine loophole
Three no-go arguments give mutually inconsistent assumptions
Realistic material properties qualitatively change the extraction conclusion vs ideal conductors

position.last_activity_desc: Project initialization complete; roadmap created with 7 phases

custom_conventions.casimir_energy_sign: E < 0 for bound configuration lower than unbounded
custom_conventions.matsubara_prime_sum: l=0 term carries half weight in primed sum notation
custom_conventions.work_sign: W_net > 0 means net energy extracted by the system; W_net <= 0 is the no-go claim
